name: Jakkur Lake: The Pioneer of Decentralized Constructed Wetlands
hero_summary: How Bengaluru transformed a dying silted cesspool into India’s flagship integrated wetland ecosystem, sustaining 200+ bird species and local traditional fisherfolk.

before.condition: Severely degraded, weed-choked water body receiving 10 MLD of raw untreated sewage from Yelahanka. Fish kills occurred seasonally with heavy silting and dry shorelines.
before.encroachment: 18.5 Acres encroached by construction debris and unauthorized fences
before.biodiversity: Less than 15 avian species spotted, commercial fishing ceased
before.community_access: Hazardous malodor, zero public access or recreational trails

after.condition: Integrated 10 MLD Secondary STP coupled with an ecological constructed wetland (macrophytes + algae ponds) filtering wastewater before it enters the main lake water body.
after.encroachment: 0.5 Acres (98% cleared, bio-fenced with native bamboo and vetiver grasses)
after.biodiversity: Over 200 species recorded, including Spot-billed Pelicans, Painted Storks, and Eurasian Spoonbills; active licensed fisherfolk cooperative harvesting 40 tonnes/year
after.community_access: 4.2 km paved pedestrian trail, open-air bird hide, community gazebos, zero foul odor

key_takeaway: Constructed wetlands act as nature-based biofilters that eliminate operating electricity costs while creating resilient urban biodiversity sanctuaries.

name: Kaikondrahalli Lake: The Gold Standard in Citizen-Led Stewardship
hero_summary: When a real estate proposal threatened to drain the lake bed into a playground, neighborhood residents banded together to create the MAPSAS trust, revitalizing 48 acres into a community sanctuary.

before.condition: Dry, cracked mud bed used for illegal municipal solid waste dumping and soil excavation. High levels of chemical runoff from Sarjapur tech corridor.
before.encroachment: 12.0 Acres occupied by illegal sheds and parking terminals
before.biodiversity: Sparrow and crow dominance only, zero nesting islands
before.community_access: Perceived as a health biohazard with rampant mosquito breeding

after.condition: Complete community-engineered rejuvenation with desilted bunds, constructed swales, 3,000 native indigenous trees, and dedicated nesting islands.
after.encroachment: 1.0 Acre (Recovered 11 acres into community green buffer)
after.biodiversity: 43 butterfly species, 120+ resident and migratory bird species, otters periodically sighted
after.community_access: Over 1,200 daily joggers, inclusive wheelchair-accessible perimeter paths, educational botanic signage

key_takeaway: Civic co-management between municipal bodies (BBMP) and citizen collectives (MAPSAS) produces higher maintenance continuity than contractor-only models.

name: Agara Lake: Transforming a Severely Polluted Basin into an Urban Lung
hero_summary: Spanning 98 acres at the critical junction of Koramangala and HSR Layout, Agara was revived through hydraulic redesign, sediment traps, and multi-tier aerators.

before.condition: Toxic algal blooms with thick cyanobacteria mats. Breached mud bunds caused monsoon street flooding along Outer Ring Road.
before.biodiversity: Severe fish asphyxiation during pre-monsoon heat waves
before.community_access: Dilapidated mud embankments with frequent anti-social incidents

after.condition: Engineered desilting, deep water retention basins, solar-powered paddle aerators, dedicated silt-trapping forebays, and restored lake islands.
after.encroachment: 1.5 Acres (Recovered and planted with Miyawaki urban forest)
after.biodiversity: Darter colonies, cormorants, purple swamphens, and flourishing freshwater fish populations
after.community_access: 5.5 km flood-lit synthetic and gravel track, open gym, nature education pavilion

key_takeaway: Combining upstream silt forebays with solar aeration prevents recurrent eutrophication while serving as an essential flood mitigation sponge.

name: Bellandur Lake: The Epic Battle Against Industrial Toxic Foam and Fires
hero_summary: Bengaluru’s largest water body, spanning 913 acres, captured global headlines when toxic hydrocarbon foam burst into flames. Here is the data-driven journey of its ongoing revival.

before.condition: Over 450 MLD of untreated municipal sewage and toxic industrial effluents caused 10-foot chemical foam clouds, frequent spontaneous methane fires, and complete ecological collapse.
before.encroachment: 148 Acres of illegal landfilling, building encroachment and debris dumping
before.biodiversity: Zero native fish survival, extreme toxic vector breeding
before.community_access: Road traffic blocked by toxic floating foam; property values in proximity plunged

after.condition: National Green Tribunal (NGT) ordered comprehensive desilting (over 3 million cubic meters of toxic sludge evacuated), diversion channels, and commissioned intermediate STPs.
after.encroachment: 77.5 Acres recovered by BBMP/BDA joint survey taskforce
after.biodiversity: Pioneer aquatic vegetation returning in peripheral channels; seasonal egrets returning
after.community_access: Foam suppressed via chemical defoamers and barrier walls; work ongoing for full public eco-park

key_takeaway: Restoring mega-catchment lakes requires strict industrial zero-liquid discharge enforcement alongside massive decentralized catchment-level sewage treatment.
